# Add bounded resident-observation subscriptions to browser and headless SDKs

Parent: #763. Astra xhigh scope; Luna max implements; Astra medium verifies concrete bugs only.

Ship browser/headless `subscribeObservations` with a shared bounded subscribe/update/read/close lifetime, using the resident values already delivered by #777. This is the smallest complete selective lifecycle slice: an app can open selected effect meters, receive current values without writing a polling/arming service, change selection atomically, and release the work when the panel closes. Scope the initial lifecycle to resident observations explicitly; do not make three unlike query implementations into a purported complete analysis stream. Keep #763 open.

## Required product contract

- Each engine provides one lazily created subscription owner, shared by its browser or headless SDK entry point. Subscribe accepts a bounded explicit selection array of stable track/rack/effect-slot/tap IDs, L/R projection, an explicit normalized observation window, and bounded delivery cadence. Use generated effect descriptors and the existing owner map. No all-track default and no new host-side DSP catalog.
- A successful subscribe/update returns effective configuration, a handle, an SDK-local owner/epoch identity, the existing command acknowledgement's real `appliedAtSample`, and admitted subscription/binding/result bounds. The SDK owner identity is not advertised as the still-missing portable engine-clock identity. Defaults are concrete in the acknowledgement. Use positive `windowBlocks` in native commands so SDK acknowledgement need not guess the native zero/default normalization.
- Validate the whole request, resolve every stable ID, reserve bounded SDK storage, and derive one existing atomic observation-command transaction before acknowledging. Failed subscribe arms nothing; failed update preserves the prior selection, cached results and references. Refuse an operation exceeding the current maximum command-record count rather than splitting its atomic transaction. No extra render command or queue design.
- Identical target/channel/window configurations share one managed binding/read and a reference count; closing one consumer leaves another alive. The current native owner has one window configuration per tap: reject conflicting simultaneous configurations with an explicit typed conflict, rather than silently changing another subscriber's semantics. Supporting concurrent different-window jobs remains in #763. A previously manually armed tap must not be silently acquired and later disarmed by this service. Serialize managed mutations with SDK console observation edits, refusing conflicting manual edits while managed; do not invent a cross-process ownership registry.
- Browser: one bounded off-render scheduling loop reads the selected union with at most one read request in flight; callback receives a synchronous notification and reads the newest value. Do not enqueue payload-bearing callback promises or add an AsyncIterator backlog. Headless: an explicit `pump()` between caller render calls performs the same bounded read; it never renders or starts a timer. Both expose `readLatest()` returning owned stable selected rows. Preserve each resident owner's native units, independent channel values, original `[firstSample,endSample)` and sequence; never borrow the aggregate meter span.
- Retain at most one latest result per managed binding and a per-handle delivery cursor. Repeated owner sequence is not a new publication. Report missed native windows from sequence deltas within one epoch separately from cached publications skipped by that consumer; first read establishes a baseline instead of claiming historical losses. Keep sample clocks and long-lived counters as bigint. No fabricated exact interval for a command or non-ready row.
- `close()` is idempotent; last close issues the existing disarm transaction and stops polling. Closure acknowledgement follows successful disarm; typed refusal is not falsely reported as success. A shared closing promise prevents duplicate disarms. Before reload/disposal/recreation, invalidate old handles and pending deliveries; late reads must never attach to a new owner with the same array positions. New owners require explicit subscription. Close/reload do not retain dead timers, listeners, result queues or ownership entries. No subscriptions means no polling or analysis traffic; resident effect computation that already happens for audio remains correctly classified as resident cost.

## Small implementation, using current code

Add one SDK core module containing selections, bounded binding/reference counts, last-result/cursor handling and lifecycle. Wire small adapters in `sdk/src/browser/engine.ts` and `sdk/src/headless/engine.ts`. Reuse `sdk/src/core/observation.ts` validation/resolution/decoding and generated `CATALOG`; reuse `EngineConsole.submit` and `ObserveSubscribe`/`ObserveUnsubscribe` (whole-batch admission and `appliedAtSample` already exist). Expose only the lifecycle needed by this resident slice; add other discriminants when their actual implementations land. No scheduler framework, new Rust analysis, generated ABI, Worker, graph observer, unsafe queue, transport, or native thread.

Add finite configurable SDK limits for handles, distinct managed bindings, selected rows and polling rate, checked before ack; reflect existing native observation preparation limits separately. Count fixed row storage and bounded object counts honestly rather than inventing exact JavaScript heap-byte claims. Keep read batches within the existing 256-row endpoint limit. Browser callbacks receive availability notifications, not an unbounded history. Public naming is Luna's routine choice.

Source evidence: `sdk/src/core/console.ts:331,347` already arms/disarms and verifies all-or-none admission; `sdk/src/core/observation.ts` resolves stable IDs and preserves owner windows; `sdk/src/browser/engine.ts:415` and `sdk/src/headless/engine.ts:130` expose the read endpoints; headless replacement/disposal is centralized in `loadSession`/`dispose`. Existing `docs/EFFECT_OBSERVATION_V1.md` and `crates/engine/src/realtime/observe.rs` define conflating levels and per-window sequences. Use that authority, not a new observation model.

## Few acceptance gates, then ship

1. Actual headless and existing Chromium/Firefox/WebKit SDK harness: subscribe to compressor + gate with distinct L/R, explicitly render/pump headlessly, observe automatic browser delivery, and retain an earlier result through later publications unchanged. Assert original bigint spans/sequence, including values above 2^53 through the existing decoder seam.
2. Invalid second target, exhausted SDK/native capacity and refused update leave every old selection and arm state intact. Two identical subscribers perform one arm/read; first close keeps it live, last close disarms. Conflicting windows/manual ownership refuse explicitly. Empty/zero-capacity owners stay idle.
3. A slow consumer has one current result and honest skips; repeated reads produce no fake publication. Closing or same-position session replacement during a delayed read cannot publish to an old/new wrong handle. No work after the final successful close, including when callbacks throw. One in-flight read and finite scheduling are asserted with existing injected host seams.
4. Run proportional SDK types/tests, existing package/export checks and the existing actual-browser qualification once at a coherent candidate. Underlying DSP/ABI is unchanged: do not add an FFT corpus, native benchmark, transport harness or new full matrix to this issue. Luna max implements; Astra medium reviews concrete contract bugs only. Root records/pushes coherent checkpoints and synchronizes the child issue; parent remains open.

## Parent obligations remain attached, not silently deferred outside #763

This closes only the first managed resident lifetime. The following remain required under #763: the common lifecycle for live response and spectrum; full effect/graph discovery and normalized effective limits; per-band/per-field selection; response state identity and change-driven recomputation/unchanged-curve suppression; identical analysis-job sharing and atomic multi-target admission; multiple prepared spectrum targets and selective updates; continuous block-aligned hop/rate, calibrated power smoothing, reset/warm-up/history epochs and gaps/underrun validity; full portable clock/plan/state/content/publication identities, parameter changes within FFT windows and honest loss accounting; native provider parity and packed additive remote vector schemas/peer compatibility; bounded SAB capture plus the qualified pooled transferable fallback and their ownership/slow-worker behavior; sample-time join with per-item age/status; resource reports, required realtime/correctness evidence, integrated browser/headless examples including one EQ and two taps, source-spectrum documentation migration, and one frozen descriptive transport comparison. Input-filter/ordered EQ subtotal work already shipped still needs final parent integration; the parent's exact coefficient, ownership and no-audio-change requirements continue to apply.

The current #781 spectrum is zero or one preparation-selected target with independent one-shot captures, no hop or smoothing; repeating it on a timer does not fulfill continuous spectrum. `BrowserEngine.querySpectrum` currently uses the engine-level AbortSignal rather than per-subscription cancellation; headless reads use preparation channels. `TrackResponseResult.snapshotToken` identifies a capture, not stable coefficient state. Those are concrete later integration seams, not reasons to build their replacements before this resident slice ships.

No owner rescope is required to ship this child: #763 expressly permits bounded staged children. Owner amendment is required before declaring launch/parent complete with only one prepared spectrum target, no continuous/smoothed stream, no SAB/qualified fallback, no packed remote vectors, no complete identity/loss envelope, no join or no transport comparison. They are binding parent scope today. Frozen-response mode, arbitrary effect taps, phase/group delay, device-clock mapping, extended-rate matrices and optimization/tooling frameworks are already authorized outside-parent successors. Do not silently use that exception for the required items above.
